statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail holds the low edge of the watch band because NQ is still trading inside an intact overnight range whose high and low were both fully retraced, while Stress stays high on a 5.25% ten-year yield, crude near 92 and a wide latest-session megacap dispersion.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the mapped state stays WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. A narrow elevated-risk window is flagged from 13:30 to 15:00 UTC, spanning the US cash open and the 14:00 UTC JOLTS and CB Consumer Confidence cluster, where the published forecast maps to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES for one hour. A second, lower checkpoint sits at the 17:00 UTC OpenAI DevDay keynote, which is modelled inside the watch band. Outside those hours the published forecast returns to the watch and low bands.
headline: NQ holds inside an intact 30,372.25-30,635.25 overnight range at 30,599.75 while the 10-year yield sits at a 2007-era high of 5.25% and crude eases to 92.28
body: NQ front-month trades 30,599.75, up 33.50 points or 0.11% against a 30,566.25 prior close, and remains inside the 30,372.25-30,635.25 overnight range established before the European session. That range has not been extended in either direction since the preceding assessment: the dip toward 30,372.25 and the push to 30,635.25 were each fully retraced, and price is currently about 35 points below the high rather than holding it. Persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks and repeated extension after failed retracements are all absent, which is the central reason Tail stays at the low edge of the watch band rather than stepping into the elevated band. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Monday at 30,276.81, down 1.08%, roughly 320 points below the current futures level. VIX is unchanged at 16.07 inside a 15.98-16.19 range, which conflicts with the macro backdrop rather than confirming it. Cross-asset evidence remains the dominant Stress input. The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.25%, the highest since 2007, with the 2-year at 4.95% and the 30-year near 5.56%; the Federal Reserve H.15 release for 25 September shows 4.81%, 5.17% and 5.49% respectively, so the move is a genuine continuation rather than a single print. WTI has eased to 92.28, down 0.35% and well off the 94.74 overnight high, after Brent topped 107 on Monday when Iran's conditional proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz was rejected; commercial transits ran 132 for 21-27 September against roughly 130 per day before the February escalation. The softening oil impulse is a modest Tail-reducing input against an otherwise high-stress regime. Shared Finviz context collected at 07:33 UTC is older than the 90-minute freshness threshold and reported a partial collection with futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it is used only as stale latest-session colour: it showed wide megacap dispersion on Monday with NVDA higher against sharp declines in META, TSLA and QCOM, consistent with verified reporting that ties Meta's drop to a rumoured competing OpenAI agent ahead of the DevDay 2026 keynote scheduled for 17:00 UTC today. Two scheduled checkpoints define the session: the 14:00 UTC stack of JOLTS Job Openings, JOLTS Job Quits and CB Consumer Confidence landing 30 minutes into the cash open, and that keynote. Neither has printed, so neither raises Tail beyond the conditional forecast hours.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hours were published. Tail ranged from 17 to 27. Exactly one single-hour excursion reached the elevated band, at 14:00 UTC on Monday, and it reverted within the following hour. Tail troughed at 17 through the late Monday and early Tuesday overnight session, stepped to 24 at 01:00, 03:00 and 04:00 UTC as the European handover approached, then settled at 20 in each of the last four hours. Stress never fell below 76 and peaked at 85 at 10:00 UTC on Monday, reflecting the persistent high-yield and high-oil regime rather than any single release. Confidence held between 86 and 88 throughout, with the last eight hours all at 88 on continuous futures price-path availability.
outlookSummary: The published forecast keeps Tail in the watch band through the European and early US session, with a single elevated-band hour at 14:00 UTC where JOLTS Job Openings, JOLTS Job Quits and CB Consumer Confidence print 30 minutes into the cash session. That stacking of the opening auction with a high-impact data cluster is the only hour mapped above the block threshold, and Tail is modelled to decay back into the watch band by 15:00 UTC on an orderly price-discovery assumption. A second checkpoint is flagged at 17:00 UTC for the scheduled OpenAI DevDay keynote, modelled at the top of the watch band on megacap AI headline risk rather than macro risk. Overnight hours into Wednesday return to the low band, then Tail steps back to the watch band from 02:00 UTC as the European handover and the final session of the quarter approach, ending at 23 in the last published hour ahead of the 30 September ADP and Core PCE releases.
